item.title: Nagarjuna: Zero to Hero
item.description:
An own-words introduction to Nagarjuna and Madhyamaka: svabhava, dependent arising, emptiness, analysis of motion and time, the two truths, self, Buddha, nirvana and later debates. Narrated by Tara, an AI voice. Original explanatory narration, not a reading of a commercial translation. Provisional interpretation, not an authoritative translation or lineage transmission. MMK verses are paraphrased; verse numbers follow the scriptwriter's memory of Sanskrit numbering and were not independently checked for this release. Historical legends, proposed Greek contacts, and disputed readings are labeled as such. Comparisons with Hume, Zeno, Wittgenstein and physics are parallels, not influence or scientific equivalence. Rangtong/shentong, ineffability and logical readings remain live debates. The Dzogchen connection is presented as a tradition's view, not as Nagarjuna's own teaching. Original narration CC0 1.0 Universal; underlying sources retain their own rights.

item.title: Lacan: Zero to Hero
item.description:
An own-words introduction to Jacques Lacan: the mirror stage, language and the unconscious, desire and lack, the Real, jouissance, clinic, critics and legacy. Narrated by Tara, an AI voice. Provisional interpretation of contested psychoanalytic theory, not medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Famous lines are paraphrased, not readings from a commercial translation. Historical anecdotes, seminar references, clinical claims, sexuation and gender interpretations, and the 2004 INSERM report remain attributed or contested claims, not settled scientific findings. The Foucault remark is a secondhand report via Searle; the closing lecture remark is loosely sourced and should not be treated as a verified quotation. Biographical dates and anecdotal details were not independently fact-checked for this release. Original narration CC0 1.0 Universal; underlying sources retain their own rights.

item.title: The Daoists: Lao Tzu and Zhuangzi: Zero to Hero
item.description:
An own-words introduction to Laozi and Zhuangzi: textual history, Dao, wu wei, water, the valley, the uncarved block, language, perspective, Cook Ding and the butterfly. Legends and disputed authorship are labeled; comparisons with Buddhism, Wittgenstein and Stoicism are interpretive parallels, not claims of influence. Chan has multiple historical sources. Narrated by Tara, an AI voice. Provisional interpretation, not an authoritative translation. No commercial translation is read verbatim. Original narration CC0 1.0 Universal; underlying sources retain their own rights. Reference notes: in chapter 3 of this audio, the war paragraph moves from Daodejing 31 (weapons and mourning) to 68 (the unaggressive warrior and angerless fighter). Guodian has different wording corresponding to received chapter 19; this does not establish that its whole anti-Confucian thrust was simply added later. The received text has 81 chapters, but divisions vary in earlier versions. Sources for these notes: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/laozi/ ; https://ctext.org/photo.pl?if=en&node=11659 ; https://daodejing.ru/en/chapters/31 . The audio's opening hour is approximate: actual runtime 72:33.
